title: reading-hopper-ivy-2026
content:
Reading Hopper — rolling personal notes (short bursts, stream-of-consciousness).

Context: quick capture after hallway convos + ACL minisymp. Not polished. Use this to seed follow-up experiments and a compact one-pager for the team.

---
Top-of-mind takeaways (TL;DR):
- Practical KV cache compression seems most promising when combined with stubbed eviction policies; storage p99 matters more than mean.
- For long-context QA, hybrid sparse-kv (only keep salient turns) + chunked retrieval reduces hallucination in my small protos.
- Microbench: measure rehydration time of compressed KV shards under 95th percentile traffic patterns (burstiness matters).

Papers skimmed / quick notes:
1) "Sparse KV Representations for Long Context" (arXiv link above)
   - Idea: compress only old entries using learned projection + cluster centroids.
   - My note: projection quality degrades non-linearly with distance — test with synthetic n-gram repeats.
   - Followup: implement lightweight PCA baseline vs learned projection to get a cheap lower bound.

2) "Latency-first continuous batching" (slide deck I saw at minisymp)
   - Idea: dynamic micro-batching with soft deadlines per customer route.
   - My note: Redwood routing could expose a per-tenant latency budget to inform batching multiplier. Could be a flag on the model route config.

3) "Prompt conditioning and staleness" (workshop paper)
   - Key: older context hurts more when model is updated (distribution shift).
   - My note: record model version on cached prefix keys and invalidate prefix cache on canary rollouts. Add to rollout checklist (see TODOs).

Experiments to try (priority sorted):
- [P0] Small local bench: compress KV cache with 8-bit product quantization and measure decode/re-hydration time for 1M tokens worth of cache; report 50/95/99 latencies. (Owner: Ivy)
- [P1] Canary-aware cache invalidation: tag cached entries with model hash; simulate canary switch and measure error rate on staged prompts. (Owner: Ravi)
- [P2] Prefix-salience filter: score chunks with cheap bi-encoder and only keep top-K segments per session. Ablate K={1,3,5}. (Owner: Mika)

Quick sketches / heuristics I keep returning to:
- Keep "hot" KV frames in raw float32, older frames in compressed store + small LRU hotset.
- Eviction should consider semantic novelty, not just recency; compute delta-embedding w.r.t. last kept.
- When serving, if compressed frame decode time > latency SLO threshold, break decode into background rehydration + serve fallback shorter prefix.

Notes to self / friction points:
- Storage cost calc: need to reconcile S3 object overhead vs local NVMe chunking for cache shards. Estimate math feels off; set up quick spreadsheet.
- Integration with rollout manager: is there an existing hook? Check infra PRs: linked_artifacts PR 87 might have the API.
- Need a reproducible small test harness (dockerized) that can load a 770M model + mock KV store to profile rehydration. Avoid full infra until we have numbers.

Meeting snippets (for later synthesis):
- Slack thread #kv-cache: @ravi mentioned multi-tenant shard packing reduces overhead but increases tail if tenant hotset mispredicted. Idea: pack hot tenants on separate NVMe pool.
- Mini workshop takeaway: ops care about predictable worst-case. Metrics should include cold-decode 99.9 and burst rehydration time.

Open questions / hypothesis list:
- H1: Using PQ (product quant) with per-shard codebooks gives better decode speed than global codebook because of locality — testable.
- H2: Semantic novelty scoring reduces total stored tokens by 3x without hurting answer fidelity for retrieval-augmented QA.
- H3: Canary rollouts without cache invalidation cause subtle hallucination regressions in ~0.5% of prompts. Worth automating a small regression check.

Concrete next steps (2-week):
1) Spin up local bench for P0 and capture decode latencies (Ivy).
2) Draft short one-pager with experiment plan + cost estimate for infra (to share in Monday sync).
3) Add cache-tagging hook to rollout checklist (PR candidate).

Fragments / snippets for the one-pager: 
- "Problem: cache staleness + storage cost leads to tradeoffs between latency and fidelity."
- "Proposal: hybrid hot/cold KV store, canary-aware invalidation, and novelty-based eviction."
- Quick metrics to collect: token-store-bytes, decode-95, decode-99.9, QA-fidelity (EM/F1), cost-per-100k-tokens.

Random TODOs (brain-dump):
- [ ] Create spreadsheet comparing PQ variants (IVY)
- [ ] Schedule 30m with infra to talk shard placement (Ravi)
- [ ] Add smoke tests for cache-invalidation during model rollouts (Mika)
- [ ] Prototype small novelty scorer (bi-encoder) and run on existing chat logs (Ivy)

Useful links I scribbled during reading: 
- arXiv: https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00926 (paper above)
- Internal PR (kv experiments): https://github.com/redwood-inference/kv-cache-experiments/pull/87
- Slack threads: https://app.slack.com/client/TXXXXXX/CYYYYYY (kv-cache)

End notes: keep this light — capture ideas fast. Will move useful stuff into a proper draft one-pager once P0 numbers exist.

— Ivy
